cellprograms

Discover cell-type-specific transcriptional programs from pseudobulk single-cell RNA-seq, and integrate them into higher-order multicellular states.

The cellprograms package fits empirical-Bayes matrix factorizations (flashier) independently within each cell type, then — only when scientifically useful — investigates how the recovered programs coordinate across cell types, share their gene loadings, and associate with context.

Major functionality of the cellprograms package:

  • as_cell_program_data() Build the validated pseudobulk data object (named list of observations x genes matrices, one per cell type)
  • fit_celltype_programs() Fit per-cell-type programs with the EBMF backend (hard residualization or soft fixed covariate adjustment; flashier or cebmf_torch backend)
  • freeze_preprocessing() / project_programs_to_cells() Freeze a fit’s preprocessing spec (MR-0) and project new samples onto its programs through a unit-checked oracle
  • assess_program_stability() Subsampling stability of recovered programs, with explicit accounting of failed refits
  • canonicalize_programs() Align program sign, scale and labels across cell types
  • program_scores() Sample x program activity matrix across all cell types
  • program_loadings() Gene x program loading matrix
  • top_genes() Top-loaded genes of a single program, with optional lfsr
  • program_summary() Per-cell-type summary: number of programs, R2, ELBO
  • find_coordinated_programs() Detect coordinated multicellular programs (CMPs) with family-wise error control by within-strata donor permutation
  • cmp_scores() Donor x CMP consensus scores
  • annotate_cmp_tf() TF footprint of every member program from CollecTRI regulons (competitive + self-contained tests)
  • cmp_triage() One-row-per-CMP triage: recurrent genes, nuisance counts, context association, replication, shared TFs
  • program_sharing() Classify matched programs as shared, partial, or private (mashr on loading posteriors)
  • artifact_genes() / flag_artifact_genes() Mask V(D)J and donor-genotype artifact genes
  • simulate_pseudobulk() Simulation with planted programs and ground truth

Installation 

remotes::install_github("mdmanurung/cellprograms")

Requires R >= 4.3. The flashier and ebnm backends are installed automatically (flashier via GitHub). The alternative cebmf_torch backend (optionally selected with fit_celltype_programs(backend = "cebmf_torch")) runs in a pinned Python environment (torch 2.7.1 + cebmf_torch); set options(cellprograms.cebmf_python_env = ...) to point at an existing environment, otherwise a basilisk environment is provisioned.

Quick start 

library(cellprograms)

# pseudobulk: named list of observations x genes matrices, one per cell type
x <- as_cell_program_data(pseudobulk, sample_metadata = metadata)
validate_cell_program_data(x)

fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x)  # max_factors = 10 default; override to revisit
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)

Z <- program_scores(fit)   # sample x cellular-program activity matrix
W <- program_loadings(fit) # gene x program loadings

Frozen preprocessing and out-of-sample projection

Fits record their full preprocessing specification, and project_programs_to_cells() refuses queries whose declared measurement units differ from the source fit’s — a projection oracle, not a silent re-derivation:

spec <- freeze_preprocessing(x, features = "variable", n_variable_genes = 2000)
fit  <- fit_celltype_programs(x, preprocessing_spec = spec,
                              feature_scale = "logcounts")
Z_new <- project_programs_to_cells(fit, new_pseudobulk,
                                   feature_scale = "logcounts")

A refit supplied with a frozen spec cannot silently drift from the frozen panel: any explicit conflict with the spec is an error. Stability (assess_program_stability()) reports how many subsample refits failed (n_failed/n_success) so that recovery frequencies are computed over successful refits, never silently diluted.

Motivation

Discover, don’t map. Unlike reference-projection tools, cellprograms identifies programs de novo within each cell type. The design principle is factorize locally first; integrate later only when scientifically useful — a B-cell program is discoverable because it explains B-cell expression, regardless of whether anything analogous happens in other cell types. Cross-cell-type coordination is investigated subsequently, never assumed.

Status

v0.2.0 — core data model, flashier backend with hard (residualize) and soft (fixed) covariate adjustment, canonicalization, a calibrated cross-cell-type sharing test (principal angles in scores space, optional blocked-permutation strata), subsampling stability, MOFAcellulaR export, and simulation utilities. Coordinated multicellular program (CMP) detection is shipped and confirmed by two pre-registered held-out benchmarks (benchmarks/cmp_detection/). Post-hoc shared-vs-specific program assessment (program_sharing(), mashr-based) and artifact-gene masking (artifact_genes(), flag_artifact_genes(), fit-time exclude_genes) are included. Integration backends such as ICA and EV-BIDIFAC were evaluated and rejected (see reports/ROADMAP.md).

Recent additions: an alternative cebmf_torch torch backend (same preprocessing and output contract; fixed residual SDs bind there, while the flashier path currently passes them through unenforced — see the var_floor docs), frozen preprocessing specifications with a unit-checked projection oracle (freeze_preprocessing(), project_programs_to_cells()), and a hardening pass across the analysis contract: stability refits account for failed subsamples explicitly, CMP member orientation propagates along the linking edges that formed the CMP, and program_sharing() validates matches= references and warns on forced pairs (“shared” means active-in-both, not proven shared structure — check p_all_shared).

Default configuration (point_laplace gene prior, per-donor residual variance, max_factors = 10) was selected by a benchmark-first optimization loop against simulation ground-truth recovery and refined by a pseudobulk tuning benchmark (below); see reports/plan_review.md and reports/final_report.md.

Tuning benchmark: why max_factors = 10?

The default configuration is grounded in a full-factorial tuning benchmark on COMBAT COVID pseudobulk (770,833 cells, 134 donors, 16 cell types), run with the same evaluators as the package (python/run_tuning_search.py in this repository):

  • Search space: 32 configs = loading prior (point_laplace, point_normal) x max_factors (10, 15, 30, 50) x var_type (0, 1) x backfit (TRUE, FALSE), on TMM + scran-HVG pseudobulk (edgeR TMM size factors, top-2000 HVGs per cell type).
  • Selection metric: mean rank of disease-status kNN (corrected macro-F1) and WHO-ordinal severity kNN Spearman, with a reconstruction guardrail (held-out R^2 >= 0.423, the MOFA2-comparator value).
  • Result: max_factors = 10 dominated every prior x variance x backfit combination. K >= 30 overfits: with 16 cell types the concatenated representation reaches 400-600 factors and disease-signal recovery collapses to ~0. The winning config (point_laplace, K=10, var_type = 1, backfit) improved disease kNN 0.255 -> 0.359 over the old K=30 default while passing the guardrail (held-out R^2 0.48-0.59 across preprocessing arms).
  • Preprocessing parity: the K-vs-biology relationship was stable across three arms (log-norm all genes, log-norm + HVG, TMM + HVG), so the default is not an artifact of one normalization.
  • var_type: 1 (one residual-variance parameter per donor) is the right default for pseudobulk. var_type = 2 (per-gene) crashes on log-normalized pseudobulk (NaN in the variance update) and is strictly worse where it runs. c(1, 2) (Kronecker rank-one) is supported but unbenchmarked at pseudobulk scale and substantially slower.
  • External validity: on an independent cohort (Stephenson, 126 donors, 43 cell types) the tuned config generalized (disease kNN 0.648 vs 0.468 for the old default) and reduced retention of technical structure (pool-ID kNN ~0.46 -> 0.21-0.24 on log-norm arms).

Benchmark artifacts (search tables, attribution, cross-dataset validation, MOFA-FLEX comparison) and the summary report are available on request; the runners live in python/.

Coordinated multicellular programs

find_coordinated_programs() finds groups of programs from different cell types whose donor-level scores co-vary (coordinated multicellular programs, CMPs), with family-wise error control by within-strata donor permutation. Gene overlap plays no role in the call; annotate_cmp_lr(), annotate_cmp_themes(), cmp_gene_overlap() and cmp_context_association() annotate called CMPs, each with its own null.

x <- as_cell_program_data(pseudobulk, sample_metadata = metadata)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit_celltype_programs(x, max_factors = 30, covariates = "site"))
res <- find_coordinated_programs(fit, strata = "site", ambient = "flag", n_perm = 999)
cmp_scores(fit, res)                      # donors x CMPs consensus scores

Use max_factors = 30 for fits intended for CMP detection. A CMP can only be called if each member program exists upstream. In the pre-registered cmp-bench-v1.2 held-out benchmark (seeds 1051-1100; 8 scenarios x 2 simulation bases; 800 datasets per arm), fitting with max_factors = 30 raised pooled membership F1 from 0.571 to 0.705 (paired difference +0.127, 95% CI 0.113-0.142), entirely on the semi-synthetic base built from Stephenson pseudobulk (0.671 -> 0.934), with every false-call guardrail <= 0.06 (null FWER 0.04 / 0.00). The global default stays at 10 because the tuning benchmark below optimizes a different target (disease signal in the concatenated representation), where K >= 30 overfits. find_coordinated_programs() prints a one-time message when a fit with max_factors < 30 has a cell type at its cap. On real cohorts (Stephenson, COMBAT), cap 30 roughly doubled the number of CMPs; many added CMPs carried immunoglobulin/TCR V genes or genes with known donor-genotype variation (e.g. GSTM1, HLA-DQ/DR haplotype genes). These may co-vary across cell types for genetic rather than biological-coordination reasons; this is unconfirmed without genotype data. Use ambient = "flag" and inspect each CMP’s top genes, cmp_context_association() and replication before interpreting it. Benchmark scripts, pre-registrations and result tables are in benchmarks/cmp_detection/.

Interpreting CMPs: TF footprints and triage 

net <- prepare_collectri(omnipath_collectri_table)   # OmniPath interactions?datasets=collectri
tf  <- annotate_cmp_tf(fit, cmp, net)                # TF footprint of every member program
tri <- cmp_triage(fit, cmp, context = "severity", covariates = c("institute", "sex"),
                  replicate_by = "institute", tf = tf)

annotate_cmp_tf() fits a univariate linear model of each member’s CMP-oriented loadings on each signed CollecTRI regulon. A TF is called in a member only if it passes both a competitive test (BH-adjusted ULM, targets vs other genes) and a self-contained sign-flip test (targets coherently signed), which stops regulons of unloaded genes from looking “depleted” in skewed programs. TFs called with one sign in >= 2 members and >= half of the members are shared (a candidate common upstream driver); specific TFs show how one cell type reads out the signal. Footprints describe which regulons a program resembles; they are not evidence that the TF causes the coordination, and they can be circular (HLA-class-II CMPs light up CIITA/RFX5 because the HLA genes are their targets).

cmp_triage() returns one row per CMP with its recurrent top genes, counts of nuisance genes (cmp_nuisance_genes(): V(D)J, candidate genotype markers, sex chromosome, immediate-early genes, platelet/erythrocyte markers), the ambient fraction, context association, within-level sign replication and shared TFs, plus a heuristic label for prioritization.

Program sharing and artifact masking

program_sharing() assesses whether programs matched across cell types share their gene loadings (mashr on the stored loading posteriors), classifying each matched group as shared, partial, or private — correlated loadings alone do not imply shared effects. flag_artifact_genes() marks programs whose top genes are V(D)J segments or known donor-genotype markers; fit_celltype_programs(..., exclude_genes = artifact_genes(genes)) removes them before variable-gene selection.

res <- program_sharing(fit, n_perm = 199, z_thresh = 1.5)
flags <- flag_artifact_genes(fit)

On the Stephenson and COMBAT COVID cohorts (K = 30), the broadest cross-cell-type “shared” program was the immunoglobulin/V(D)J artifact program (ambient/clonal leakage), while interferon and cell-cycle programs replicated as genuinely shared across both cohorts — mask artifact genes before interpreting sharing.
